Brain injury? Um... no, I've never hit my head that hard or had any neurological stuff. And I was still completely sure that the old ticketing software at work was flagging my account. So the mood stuff was fine, but the other stuff was definitely still happening.\n\nDoctor: Have you found yourself holding the same body position for a long time, even when it would be uncomfortable?\n\nPatient: Um... holding the same position? I mean, I guess sometimes when I get really overwhelmed with everything, I'll kind of just freeze up. Like, I'll catch myself standing in the kitchen with my coffee mug just hovering halfway to my mouth, and I won't even realize how long I've been standing there. Or I'll start walking this same little loop back and forth by the couch for no real reason. I actually got that couch at a thrift store, believe it or not. It's this really cool mid-century modern style, kind of a mustard yellow color. Mark hated it when I first brought it home. He said it looked like it belonged in a 1970s bowling alley, but I think it gives the living room character. Plus, it's surprisingly comfortable once you break it in. The only problem is the fabric is a magnet for pet hair, which is weird because I don't even have any pets. But somehow, every time I sit down in black sweatpants, I stand up looking like I just hugged a golden retriever. I've gone through so many of those sticky lint rollers. The ones from the dollar store are terrible, by the way. The paper just rips in these tiny diagonal strips instead of peeling off in one clean sheet, so you spend ten minutes just trying to find the edge. It's infuriating. But yeah, sometimes I just stand there with my coffee, or do the pacing thing by the couch when things feel like too much.\n\nDoctor: Has anyone noticed that you resist when they try to move your body or get you to do something, even when you’re able to move?\n\nPatient: Resist when they try to move me? Um... no, I don't think so. I mean, nobody's really tried to physically move me around like that. I live by myself, so there's not really anyone around to do that anyway. It's just me and the apartment, which honestly is getting a little cramped. I've been thinking about trying to find a bigger place, maybe something with a balcony. I saw this one listing online the other day that had this amazing little terrace overlooking a courtyard, but the rent was just outrageous. It's crazy how much they charge for a tiny square of outdoor space in this city. And the deposit they wanted was equal to two months' rent, plus a non-refundable application fee. Application fees are such a scam. You pay fifty bucks just for them to run a credit check that costs them like two dollars, and then they don't even call you back if they pick someone else. I had a friend who spent almost three hundred dollars just applying to places before she finally got one. She works at a bakery downtown—well, she used to, before they downsized. She made these amazing sourdough loaves. Sourdough is so tricky to get right, you have to feed the starter every day and keep it at the perfect temperature. If it gets too cold, the yeast just kind of goes to sleep and the bread turns out flat. I tried making it once during that phase when everyone was baking bread, but my starter just smelled like old gym socks, so I threw it out. But anyway, no, nobody has tried to physically move me or anything like that. I just do my own thing.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever had a time when you felt unusually important or powerful?\n\nPatient: Important or powerful? No, definitely not. I mean, I'm just a customer service rep, you know? You pretty much feel like the least important person on the planet when you're doing that job. People call in and yell at you over the smallest things, acting like *they're* the king of the world. Like this one guy last week, he was screaming at me because his account update was delayed by an hour. An hour! And it's not like I personally control the servers. \n\nSpeaking of servers, my laptop has been acting so weird lately. The fan just spins up and sounds like an airplane taking off, even when I only have one browser tab open. I think it might be full of dust. I tried to buy one of those cans of compressed air to clean it out, but they lock them up behind glass at the pharmacy now. You have to press a little red button and wait for an employee to come unlock it. I stood there for like fifteen minutes the other day, pressing the button, and the overhead speaker just kept saying \"Customer assistance needed in aisle four.\" Over and over. Nobody ever came. I ended up just giving up and buying a candy bar at the front register instead. It was one of those ones with the almonds in it. I usually prefer peanuts, but peanuts have been giving me heartburn lately. Actually, almost everything gives me heartburn lately, which sucks because I love spicy food. There's this great Thai place down the street... \n\nWait, what were you asking me? Oh, right, feeling powerful. Yeah, no, I don't get feelings like that. I'm just a regular guy.\n\nDoctor: Have the voices and your certainty that the work software was flagging you been going on for at least a month?\n\nPatient: Um, a month? No, it's been a lot longer than that. I think... yeah, it's been about a year and eight months now that I've been hearing them and knowing the software is watching me. And it's not just when I'm feeling really down or anything, it's just kind of always there. \n\nLike, even when I had that brief period where I tried to get back into running—which didn't last long, by the way. I bought these really expensive running shoes, the kind with the extra thick foam on the bottom that are supposed to be like running on clouds. They were neon green. I thought maybe a bright color would motivate me to put them on in the mornings. But the laces were those weird elastic ones that you don't tie, you just pull them tight with a little plastic toggle thing. I could never get the tension right. They were either cutting off the circulation to my toes or slipping off my heel with every step. I ended up getting this massive blister on my right heel after just two miles. Blisters are the worst, especially when you have to wear dress shoes for a cousin's wedding or something. My cousin Sarah got married last October in this beautiful outdoor ceremony, but it rained the whole time. They had to rent this huge tent at the last minute, and the ground was so muddy. Everyone's shoes were ruined. They had a taco bar for the reception, though, which was pretty cool. I love tacos, especially the al pastor kind with the little pieces of pineapple mixed in. The sweetness really balances out the spice. \n\nBut yeah, anyway... what was I saying? Oh, right, the voices and the software thing. Yeah, it's been going on for like a year and eight months, not just when I'm super depressed.\n\nDoctor: Do you ever go completely mute and stop speaking for a while, even when people are talking to you?\n\nPatient: Go mute? Like, just stop talking entirely? No, I don't think so. I mean, I talk all day for my job, so I can't really get away with that. Though sometimes I definitely wish I could just hit a mute button on myself, or on the customers. My throat gets so dry by the end of my shift. I started drinking that throat coat tea, the one with the slippery elm in it? It's supposed to be really good for your vocal cords, but it tastes exactly like black licorice. \n\nI absolutely hate black licorice. When I was a kid, my grandma used to keep this crystal bowl of black jelly beans on her coffee table. Who even likes the black jelly beans? They just sat there for years, I swear they were practically fossilized. Her house always smelled like mothballs and peppermint. She had this massive grandfather clock in the hallway that chimed every fifteen minutes, day and night. It drove me crazy when I had to sleep over. The pendulum was made of this really shiny brass, and I remember trying to polish it with my sleeve once. Brass tarnishes so fast if you don't keep up with it. I have a brass lamp on my desk right now, actually, and it's looking pretty dull. I should probably buy some Brasso. You can get it at the hardware store, but the mom-and-pop hardware store near my apartment just closed down last month. They're turning it into a boutique pet bakery. A bakery for dogs! Can you believe people spend eight dollars on a cupcake for a pug? It's wild. \n\nBut anyway... no, I don't ever just go completely mute. I always answer when people talk to me, even if it's just to say yeah or whatever.\n\nDoctor: Have you lost interest in being around other people?\n\nPatient: Lost interest? I guess... I mean, my friends keep telling me I sound totally flat these days, like I'm hard to read or something. And even when they're talking about stuff I actually care about, I just end up giving these really short answers and I avoid making plans to hang out. \n\nMaking plans is just so exhausting anyway. You have to coordinate schedules, and then someone always cancels at the last minute because they forgot they had a dentist appointment. I hate the dentist. The last time I went, the hygienist kept talking to me while she had her hands in my mouth. How are you supposed to answer when someone has a metal hook scraping your molars? She was telling me all about her son's travel baseball team. Travel sports are so intense now. Parents spend thousands of dollars just so their ten-year-old can play in tournaments three states away every weekend. It's ridiculous. I played little league when I was a kid, but we just played at the park down the street. The snack shack there had the best soft pretzels. They were always super salty, and they came with this little plastic cup of neon yellow cheese. I used to dip my pretzels in it until the cheese was totally gone, and then I'd try to scrape the rest out with my finger. You can't really get good pretzels like that anymore, except maybe at the mall. But the mall is always so crowded, especially around the holidays. The parking lot is a nightmare... \n\nWait, what did you ask me? Oh, right, being around people. Yeah, I just kind of keep to myself and give short answers now. I don't really make plans with anyone.\n\nDoctor: When you freeze like that, do you stay in the exact same position for a long time even if it becomes uncomfortable?\n\nPatient: Freeze in the same position? I mean... I don't know about staying completely frozen like a statue for a really long time. But when I get really overwhelmed with everything, I do catch myself doing weird things. Like, I'll be standing in the kitchen with my coffee mug just hovering halfway to my mouth, just kind of stuck there. Or I'll find myself walking the exact same little loop around my couch over and over for no real reason. \n\nMy couch is this dark gray sectional I got off Craigslist a couple years ago. The guy who sold it to me said it was barely used, but there's definitely a dip in the middle cushion where you can tell someone sat all the time. It came with these terrible mustard yellow throw pillows that I immediately threw in the closet. Mustard yellow is just such an aggressive color, you know? It reminds me of the uniform I had to wear at my first job in high school. I worked at this hot dog stand at the local fairgrounds. We had to wear these bright yellow polo shirts with a cartoon hot dog embroidered on the pocket. The hot dog was wearing sunglasses and giving a thumbs up. It was so embarrassing. The worst part was that the stand didn't have air conditioning, and in August it would get up to like a hundred degrees in there. The smell of boiling hot dogs and stale buns just baked into my clothes. I must have washed that uniform a hundred times, but I could never get the smell out. I actually had to throw the shirts away when I quit because even my mom said they were making the whole laundry room smell like cheap meat. I haven't been able to eat a hot dog since then. \n\nBut yeah, what were we talking about? Oh, freezing. Yeah, I just kind of get stuck holding my coffee or pacing around the couch sometimes when it's all too much.\n\nDoctor: Has anyone ever placed your arms or body into a position and then you stayed that way for a while?\n\nPatient: Placed my arms in a position? Like... like someone else moving my body for me? No, nobody does that. I live by myself, so there's no one around to even try that, you know? It's just me and my cat, Barnaby. \n\nBarnaby is a Maine Coon mix, so he's absolutely massive. He's got these giant tufted ears and paws the size of baseballs. He's actually the reason I had to buy a new vacuum cleaner last month. He sheds so much, it's like a second cat is forming on my rug every week. I ended up getting one of those Dyson stick vacuums. They're so expensive, but everyone says they're the best. I don't know though, the battery only lasts like twenty minutes on the highest setting. By the time I finish the living room and the hallway, it's dead. Then I have to wait three hours for it to charge just so I can do my bedroom. It's so annoying. I should have just bought a regular plug-in one. My mom has this old Hoover from the nineties that still works perfectly. It's this ugly teal color, and it's super loud, but it sucks up everything. She used to make me vacuum the stairs every Saturday morning when I was a teenager. The cord was never quite long enough to reach all the way to the top, so I always had to unplug it halfway up and find another outlet. We lived in this split-level house, and the layout was just so weird. The kitchen was basically on a landing between the living room and the bedrooms...\n\nWait, sorry. No, nobody poses my arms or anything like that. I just move myself.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever repeated other people's words exactly after they say them?\n\nPatient: Repeated other people's words? Like, repeating them back? No, I don't think I do that. Unless you count when I'm on the phone at work. I work in customer service for this internet provider, and we actually have to repeat the customer's issue back to them as part of our script. It's supposed to show \"active listening\" or whatever. So if they say, \"My router keeps dropping the signal,\" I have to say, \"I understand your router keeps dropping the signal.\" \n\nIt honestly just makes people mad half the time. They think I'm being condescending. People get so angry about their internet. I had this one guy yell at me for twenty minutes last week because his Netflix was buffering. He kept saying he paid for high speed and I was personally stealing from him. He lived out in this super rural area, too. Like, you can't live in the middle of a forest and expect gigabit speeds, you know? I actually went camping in a forest once, up in the mountains. It was supposed to be this relaxing weekend, but it rained the entire time. The tent leaked, and all my extra socks got soaked. There is nothing worse than wet socks. We tried to make a fire, but the wood was completely saturated. We ended up just sitting in my friend's car eating cold cans of baked beans and listening to the radio. They were playing this weird marathon of 80s synth-pop... \n\nBut no, I don't just repeat what people say to me in normal life. Just when my boss makes me."
